``` {r FUNCTIONS}
# Create all Functions necessary for Report

### Filter Functions ###
# Survey
FilterFunction1 <- function(data) {
  data %>% 
    mutate(TripDate = as.Date(substring(QuadratID, 8, 15), format = "%Y%m%d"),
           FixedLocationID = substring(QuadratID, 19, 22),
           Year = year(TripDate)) %>%
    left_join(FixedLocations1, by = c("FixedLocationID")) %>%
    mutate(TimeSinceCultched = as.numeric(interval(DateLastCultched, TripDate), "years")) %>%
    mutate(ProjectGroup = case_when(
      grepl("RESTORE", StationName) ~ "RESTORE-2017",
      grepl("NFWF", StationName) & Year < 2019 ~ "NFWF-2015",
      grepl("SBM Hotel", StationName) | grepl("SBM Bulkhead", StationName) ~ "Historic Uncultched",
      grepl("SBM", StationName) & Year >= 2021 & TimeSinceCultched > 0 ~ "NFWF-2021",
      grepl("NFWF21", StationName) ~ "NFWF-2021",
      grepl("NFWF24-25", StationName) | grepl("NFWF24-26", StationName) ~ "NFWF-2024 General",
      grepl("NFWF24", StationName) ~ "NFWF-2024 Pilot",
      grepl("Intertidal", ParcelName) ~ "Intertidal",
      TRUE ~ "Historic Uncultched")) 
}
###

### Survey Functions ###
summarise_ALL <- function(data) {
  summarised_data <- data %>%
    summarise(NumLiveMean_raw = mean(NumLive, na.rm = TRUE),
              NumLiveSD_raw = sd(NumLive, na.rm = TRUE),
              NumDrillsMean_raw = mean(NumDrills, na.rm = TRUE),
              NumDrillsSD_raw = sd(NumDrills, na.rm = TRUE),
              NumLegalMean_raw = mean(NumLegal, na.rm = TRUE),
              NumLegalSD_raw = sd(NumLegal, na.rm = TRUE),
              TotalWeightMean_raw = mean(TotalWeight, na.rm = TRUE),
              TotalWeightSD_raw = sd(TotalWeight, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(NumLiveDensityMean_raw = NumLiveMean_raw * 4,
           NumLiveDensitySD_raw = NumLiveSD_raw * 4,
           NumDrillDensityMean_raw = NumDrillsMean_raw * 4,
           NumDrillDensitySD_raw = NumDrillsSD_raw * 4,
           NumLegalDensityMean_raw = NumLegalMean_raw * 4,
           NumLegalDensitySD_raw = NumLegalSD_raw * 4,
           TotalWeightDensityMean_raw = TotalWeightMean_raw * 4,
           TotalWeightDensitySD_raw = TotalWeightSD_raw * 4)
  return(summarised_data)
}

###

### Plot Functions
  # Function to generate grouped bar plots with SD bars
  # df is short for data frame
generate_grouped_plot <- function(df, x_variable, x_label, y_variable, y_label, y_SD, UseColor, UseFill, title) {
  
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(Upper = !!sym(y_variable) + !!sym(y_SD))
  max_upper <- max(ungroup(df) %>%
                     dplyr::select(Upper), na.rm = TRUE)
  
  plot_list <- df %>% 
    ggplot(aes(x = factor(!!sym(x_variable), levels = unique(!!sym(x_variable))), 
               y = !!sym(y_variable), 
               color = !!sym(UseColor), 
               fill = as.factor(!!sym(UseFill)))) + 
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", 
             position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
             color = "black") + 
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = !!sym(y_variable), ymax = Upper), 
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), 
                  width = 0.25, color = "black") + 
    scale_x_discrete(x_label, expand = c(0.005, 0), 
                     guide = guide_axis(angle = -45)) +
    scale_y_continuous(y_label, expand = c(0, 0),
                       limits = c(0, ceiling(max_upper * 1.05)),
                       breaks = pretty(0:2 * ceiling(max(ungroup(df) %>% 
                                                           dplyr::select(Upper), na.rm = TRUE) / 2))) + 
    ggtitle(title) + 
    BaseForm +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom",
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0, vjust = 0)) 
  
  return(plot_list)
}
```

```{r DatabaseDownload}
# Load Database Data
# Connect to Local database server and pull all necessary data, then close connection 
con <- dbConnect(odbc(),
                 Driver = "SQL Server", 
                 Server = Server,
                 Database = Database,
                 Authentication = "ActiveDirectoryIntegrated")

# Load Fixed location information
dboFixedLocations <- tbl(con,in_schema("dbo", "FixedLocations")) %>%
  collect() %>% 
  filter(Estuary %in% Estuaries)

# Load Survey Data
hsdbSurveyQuadrat <- tbl(con,in_schema("hsdb", "SurveyQuadrat")) %>%
  collect() %>%
  filter(substring(SampleEventID, 1, 2) %in% Estuaries)

hsdbSurveySH <- tbl(con,in_schema("hsdb", "SurveySH")) %>%
  collect() %>%
  mutate(ShellHeight = as.integer(ShellHeight)) %>%
  filter(substring(QuadratID, 1, 2) %in% Estuaries)

# Disconnect from database
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)

# Remove connection
rm(con)
```

``` {r BasicStats}
### Set Project Group order to display
ProjectGroupOrder <- c("NFWF-2024", "NFWF-2024 Pilot", "NFWF-2024 General", "NFWF-2024 General Adjusted",
                       "Pilot HIGH", "Pilot LOW", "General", "General Adjusted")
QuadStats <- Quadrats_ALL %>%
  # remove erroneous samples from NFWF-2024 General where sampling occurred where no cultching had occurred
  filter(!str_detect(QuadratID, "ABSRVY_20260613_1_0525_1"))
ShellHeights_1 <- ShellHeights_ALL %>%
  # remove erroneous samples from NFWF-2024 General where sampling occurred where no cultching had occurred
  filter(!str_detect(QuadratID, "ABSRVY_20260613_1_0525_1")) 

# Prep data frame for creating SH distribution histogram 
ShellHeights_2 <- ShellHeights_1 %>%
  filter(!is.na(ShellHeight)) %>%
  mutate(Treatment = case_when(
      StationNumber == 525 ~ "NFWF-2024-Cat-Point",
      StationNumber == 526 ~ "NFWF-2024-Easthole",
      CultchDensity == 1600 ~ "Low-Relief",
      CultchDensity == 3200 ~ "High-Relief",
      TRUE ~ "ERROR")) %>%
  mutate(ShellHeightBin = cut(ShellHeight, 
                              breaks = seq(0, ceiling(max(ShellHeight, na.rm = TRUE)) + 5, by = 5),
                              right = TRUE,
                              include.lowest = TRUE)) %>% # puts measures in 5 mm bins
  group_by(Treatment) %>%
  mutate(ProjectTotal = n()) %>%
  group_by(Treatment, ShellHeightBin, ProjectTotal) %>%
  summarise(ProjectNumberMeasured = n()) %>%
  mutate(PercentMeasured = (ProjectNumberMeasured / ProjectTotal) * 100)

# Determine number of oysters measured during ReportYear
ShellHeightsReportYr <- ShellHeights_1 %>%
  filter(!is.na(ShellHeight)) 
# Determine size of largest oyster measure during ReportYear 
maxSH <- max(ShellHeightsReportYr$ShellHeight, na.rm = TRUE)

```

``` {r NFWF-2024 General Explore, eval = FALSE}
# Exploring the NFWF-2024 General data to see if TotalWeight, NumLive, and ShellHeight data was affected by the 2026 Easthole Mortality Event.
### 
# Findings: TotalWeight differences were significant, but just barely, so will be treated together. NumLive differences were NOT significant, so will be treated together. ShellHeight differences were HIGHLY significant, so will not be treated together.
###

# Filter data frames for basic stats
Qexplore <- QuadStats %>%
  filter(ProjectGroup == "NFWF-2024 General")
SHexplore <- ShellHeights_1 %>%
  filter(ProjectGroup == "NFWF-2024 General")

# Total Weight Summary by station name and Overall
TWstation_summary <- Qexplore %>%
  group_by(StationName) %>%
  summarise(
    meanTW   = mean(TotalWeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_TW    = sd(TotalWeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    medianTW = median(TotalWeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    maxTW    = max(TotalWeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    minTW    = min(TotalWeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    meanNL   = mean(NumLive, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_NL    = sd(NumLive, na.rm = TRUE),
    medianNL = median(NumLive, na.rm = TRUE),
    maxNL    = max(NumLive, na.rm = TRUE),
    minNL    = min(NumLive, na.rm = TRUE))
              
TWoverall_summary <- Qexplore %>%
  summarise(
    StationName = "Overall",
    meanTW   = mean(TotalWeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_TW    = sd(TotalWeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    medianTW = median(TotalWeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    maxTW    = max(TotalWeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    minTW    = min(TotalWeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    meanNL   = mean(NumLive, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_NL    = sd(NumLive, na.rm = TRUE),
    medianNL = median(NumLive, na.rm = TRUE),
    maxNL    = max(NumLive, na.rm = TRUE),
    minNL    = min(NumLive, na.rm = TRUE))

# Combine both summaries into one table
TW_report <- bind_rows(TWstation_summary, TWoverall_summary)

# ShellHeight Summary by station name
SHstation_summary <- SHexplore %>%
  group_by(StationName) %>%
  summarise(
    meanSH   = mean(ShellHeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_SH    = sd(ShellHeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    medianSH = median(ShellHeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    maxSH    = max(ShellHeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    minSH    = min(ShellHeight, na.rm = TRUE))
              
SHoverall_summary <- SHexplore %>%
  summarise(
    StationName = "Overall",
    meanSH   = mean(ShellHeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_SH    = sd(ShellHeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    medianSH = median(ShellHeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    maxSH    = max(ShellHeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    minSH    = min(ShellHeight, na.rm = TRUE))

# Combine both summaries into one table
SH_report <- bind_rows(SHstation_summary, SHoverall_summary)

# Combine both reports into a single FINAL Report & delete intermediate
FINAL_report_NFWF2024General <- left_join(TW_report, SH_report, by = "StationName")
rm(TWstation_summary, TWoverall_summary, TW_report, SHstation_summary, SHoverall_summary, SH_report)

# Determine if Cat Point and Easthole data is statistically different
# Total Weight
# Check if variances are equal
var_testTW <- var.test(TotalWeight ~ StationName, data = Qexplore)
print(var_testTW)
# Since variances are equal (p = 0.433), perform t-test
t_test_equalTW <- t.test(TotalWeight ~ StationName, data = Qexplore, var.equal = TRUE)
print(t_test_equalTW)
# p = 0.044, which is statistically significant, but just barely, no data filtering needed

# NumLive
# Check if variances are equal
var_testNL <- var.test(NumLive ~ StationName, data = Qexplore)
print(var_testNL)
# Since variances are equal (p = 0.191), perform t-test
t_test_equalNL <- t.test(NumLive ~ StationName, data = Qexplore, var.equal = TRUE)
print(t_test_equalNL)
# p = 0.931, which is NOT statistically significant, no data filtering needed

# Check if variances are equal
var_testSH <- var.test(ShellHeight ~ StationName, data = SHexplore)
print(var_testSH)
# Since variances ARE NOT equal (p < 0.001), perform Welch's t-test, which is the safer default in R
t_test_welchSH <- t.test(ShellHeight ~ StationName, data = SHexplore, var.equal = FALSE)
print(t_test_welchSH)
# p < 0.001, which is HIGHLY statistically significant, These should not be treated together
```

``` {r TotalWeight Model selection, eval = FALSE}
# Figure out which data distribution to use
# ALL
# NFWF-2024 All
hist(subset(QuadStats, str_detect(ProjectGroup, "NFWF-2024"))$TotalWeight) 
# normal, range 0 - 30, strong peak at 12; 

# NFWF-2024 General
hist(subset(QuadStats, ProjectGroup == "NFWF-2024 General")$TotalWeight) 
# normal, range 5 - 20, strong peak at 14; 

# NFWF-2024 Pilot
hist(subset(QuadStats, ProjectGroup == "NFWF-2024 Pilot")$TotalWeight) 
# normal, range 0 - 30, peak at 12

# Pilot HIGH
hist(subset(QuadStats, CultchDensity == 3200)$TotalWeight)
# normal, range 5 - 30, peak at 12

# Pilot LOW
hist(subset(QuadStats, CultchDensity == 1600)$TotalWeight)
# normal, range 0 - 30, peak at 12

#############
##### Distributions, ranges, and peaks are all the same. OK to model together
#############

### NFWF-2024 ALL Model ###
## Choose distribution family
TotalWeight_NFWF_2024_gamma <- glmmTMB(TotalWeight ~ 1, 
                      family = Gamma(link = "log"), 
                      data = QuadStats)
TotalWeight_NFWF_2024_gaussian <- glmmTMB(TotalWeight ~ 1, 
                      family = gaussian(link = "identity"), 
                      data = QuadStats)
# Check goodness of fit
simulateResiduals(TotalWeight_NFWF_2024_gamma, n = 1000, plot = T)
simulateResiduals(TotalWeight_NFWF_2024_gaussian, n = 1000, plot = T)
AIC(TotalWeight_NFWF_2024_gamma, TotalWeight_NFWF_2024_gaussian)
## Gamma has good fit and AIC

## Add effects
TotalWeight_NFWF_2024_gamma_CD <- glmmTMB(TotalWeight ~ CultchDensity, 
                      family = Gamma(link = "log"), 
                      data = QuadStats)
TotalWeight_NFWF_2024_gamma_CDfactor <- glmmTMB(TotalWeight ~ factor(CultchDensity), 
                      family = Gamma(link = "log"), 
                      data = QuadStats)
TotalWeight_NFWF_2024_gamma_CD_random <- glmmTMB(TotalWeight ~ CultchDensity + (1 | FixedLocationID), 
                      family = Gamma(link = "log"), 
                      data = QuadStats)
TotalWeight_NFWF_2024_gamma_CDfactor_random <- glmmTMB(TotalWeight ~ factor(CultchDensity) + (1 | FixedLocationID), # BEST
                      family = Gamma(link = "log"), 
                      data = QuadStats)
# Check goodness of fit
simulateResiduals(TotalWeight_NFWF_2024_gamma_CD, n = 1000, plot = T)
simulateResiduals(TotalWeight_NFWF_2024_gamma_CDfactor, n = 1000, plot = T)
simulateResiduals(TotalWeight_NFWF_2024_gamma_CD_random, n = 1000, plot = T)
simulateResiduals(TotalWeight_NFWF_2024_gamma_CDfactor_random, n = 1000, plot = T)
AIC(TotalWeight_NFWF_2024_gamma_CD, TotalWeight_NFWF_2024_gamma_CDfactor, TotalWeight_NFWF_2024_gamma_CD_random, TotalWeight_NFWF_2024_gamma_CDfactor_random)
## Adding FixedLocation as a random (not fixed) effect helps and allows us to make larger generalizations; Treating CultchDensity as a factor improves fit

# post-hoc test
# 1. Get estimated marginal means (on the original response scale)
em_cultch <- emmeans(TotalWeight_NFWF_2024, ~ factor(CultchDensity), type = "response")

# 2. Perform pairwise comparisons with a Tukey adjustment
pairwise_comparisons <- pairs(em_cultch, adjust = "tukey")

# View the results
print(em_cultch)
print(pairwise_comparisons)

# Convert comparisons to a dataframe and display
pairwise_comparisons %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  kable(digits = 3, 
        caption = "Comparison of Substrate Density Across Different Treatments")

# "Post-hoc pairwise comparisons using Tukey's honest significant difference (HSD) adjustment revealed no statistically significant differences in total oyster weight among any of the tested cultch densities (all p > 0.05). The highest estimated average weight occurred at a cultch density of 1,600 (Mean = 16.3 ± 1.47), followed by 3,200 (Mean = 14.6 ± 1.31) and 800 (Mean = 12.5 ± 1.52). While oysters at a density of 1,600 were approximately 12.2% heavier than those at a density of 3,200 (Ratio = 1.122), this difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.639), suggesting that increasing cultch density beyond 1,600 yields no additional weight accumulation benefit."

```

``` {r TotalWeight Models and Dataframes}
###############
### Create model
###############

### NFWF-2024 ALL Model ###
TotalWeight_NFWF_2024 <- glmmTMB(TotalWeight ~ factor(CultchDensity) + (1 | FixedLocationID), # BEST
                      family = Gamma(link = "log"), 
                      data = QuadStats)
# Check goodness of fit & summary
simulateResiduals(TotalWeight_NFWF_2024, n = 1000, plot = T)
summary(TotalWeight_NFWF_2024)


###############
### Create dataframes to store values for plots and tables 
###############

# Generate Modeled Means, CI, and SE
# emmeans needed to extract values of Random effects
TotalWeightStats_Subtidal_modeled <- emmeans(TotalWeight_NFWF_2024, ~ CultchDensity, type = "response") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename(TotalWeightMean_modeled = response,
         TotalWeightLower_modeled = asymp.LCL,
         TotalWeightUpper_modeled = asymp.UCL) %>%
  mutate(TotalWeightMeanDensity_modeled = round((TotalWeightMean_modeled * 4), 1),
         TotalWeightLowerDensity_modeled = round((TotalWeightLower_modeled * 4), 1),
         TotalWeightUpperDensity_modeled = round((TotalWeightUpper_modeled * 4), 1)) %>%
  select(-df) %>%
  mutate(TotalWeightUpperDensity_modeled = case_when(
    TotalWeightMean_modeled <= 0 ~ 0,
    TRUE ~ TotalWeightUpperDensity_modeled))

# Generate raw mean and SD
TotalWeightStats_Subtidal_RAW <- QuadStats %>%
  group_by(CultchDensity) %>%
  summarise_ALL() %>%
  arrange(CultchDensity) %>%
  select(-matches("Num"))

# Combine into single table and remove intermediate dataframes
TotalWeightStats_Subtidal_ALL <- left_join(TotalWeightStats_Subtidal_modeled, 
                              TotalWeightStats_Subtidal_RAW, 
                              by = c("CultchDensity")) 



```

``` {r NumLive Model selection, eval = FALSE}
# Figure out which data distribution to use
# ALL
# NFWF-2024 All
hist(subset(QuadStats, str_detect(ProjectGroup, "NFWF-2024"))$NumLive) 
# nbinom, range 0 - 1000, strong peak at 100; 

# NFWF-2024 General
hist(subset(QuadStats, ProjectGroup == "NFWF-2024 General")$NumLive) 
# normal, range 50 - 300, strong peak at 175; 

# NFWF-2024 Pilot
hist(subset(QuadStats, ProjectGroup == "NFWF-2024 Pilot")$NumLive) 
# nbinom, range 0 - 1000, strong peak at 250;

# Pilot HIGH
hist(subset(QuadStats, CultchDensity == 3200)$NumLive)
# nbinom, range 150 - 1000, strong peak at 250;

# Pilot LOW
hist(subset(QuadStats, CultchDensity == 1600)$NumLive)
# normal, range 0 - 1000, peak at 400

#############
##### a variety of distributions, though not strong. Ranges (except General), and peaks are all the same. More info needed to justify modeling together
#############

### Testing pooled vs. cultch density-specific means
# Model A (pooled)
m_pooled <- glmmTMB(NumLive ~ 1,
                    family = nbinom2,
                    data = QuadStats)
simulateResiduals(m_pooled, n = 1000, plot = T)
# Model B (reef-specific means)
m_CD_Specific <- glmmTMB(NumLive ~ factor(CultchDensity),
                     family = nbinom2,
                     data = QuadStats)
simulateResiduals(m_CD_Specific, n = 1000, plot = T)
# Model C (ProjectGroup-specific means)
m_Project_Specific <- glmmTMB(NumLive ~ ProjectGroup,
                     family = nbinom2,
                     data = QuadStats)
simulateResiduals(m_Project_Specific, n = 1000, plot = T)
# Model D Additive Control
m_combined <- glmmTMB(NumLive ~ factor(CultchDensity) + ProjectGroup,
                       family = nbinom2,
                       data = QuadStats)
simulateResiduals(m_combined, n = 1000, plot = T)
# Model E
m_CD_weighted <- glmmTMB(NumLive ~ factor(CultchDensity),
                          dispformula = ~ factor(CultchDensity), # Solves the Levene test variance shift
                          family = nbinom2,
                          data = QuadStats)
simulateResiduals(m_CD_weighted, n = 1000, plot = T)

# Compared 
anova(m_pooled, m_CD_Specific, m_Project_Specific, m_combined, m_CD_weighted)
#### "Initial diagnostic plots revealed significant heteroscedasticity across groups (Levene's Test, p < 0.05). To account for this, we updated our negative binomial generalized linear model (m_CD_weighted) to explicitly model the dispersion parameter as a function of cultch density (dispformula = ~ factor(CultchDensity)). A likelihood ratio test confirmed this significantly improved overall model fit (\(\chi ^{2}\) = 18.52, df = 2, p < 0.001), successfully resolving the variance heterogeneity (Levene's Test, p > 0.05) and yielding the most parsimonious model with the lowest overall information criteria (AIC = 1415.2)."

summary(m_CD_weighted)

# post-hoc test
# 1. Get estimated marginal means (on the original response scale)
Live_em_cultch <- emmeans(m_CD_weighted, ~ factor(CultchDensity), type = "response")

# 2. Perform pairwise comparisons with a Tukey adjustment
Live_pairwise_comparisons <- pairs(Live_em_cultch, adjust = "tukey")

# View the results
print(Live_em_cultch)
print(Live_pairwise_comparisons)

# Convert comparisons to a dataframe and display
Live_pairwise_comparisons %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "omparison of Live Counts Across Different Treatments")

# "The final weighted negative binomial model revealed that cultch density exerts a profound effect on both the abundance and the spatial distribution of live oysters (\(NumLive\)). Increasing cultch density from 800 to 1,600 resulted in a highly significant, 2.6-fold increase in live oyster abundance (\(p < 0.001\)), elevating the estimated mean count from 159 (95% CI: 143–177) to 414 (95% CI: 340–505) oysters per quadrat.
# However, doubling the cultch density further to 3,200 yielded diminishing returns, resulting in an estimated mean of 430 oysters (95% CI: 364–507)—a value statistically indistinguishable from the 1,600 treatment (Ratio = 0.965, \(p = 0.960\)).
# Concurrently, the dispersion sub-model indicated that higher cultch densities significantly increased environmental overdispersion (\(p < 0.001\) for both 1,600 and 3,200 treatments). This indicates that while higher cultch availability drastically expands overall settlement capacity, it promotes a highly clustered, patchy spatial distribution of live oysters across the reef matrix compared to the more uniform, low-density baseline."


# "Although a localized mortality event occurred in one 800-density replicate two months prior to sampling, it did not significantly alter final live oyster abundance relative to its companion replicate (\(p = 0.93\)). However, the event significantly altered population structure, resulting in radically different size distributions among survivors (\(p < 0.0001\)). This decoupling of abundance and size highlights that while final numerical carrying capacity may be consistently constrained at lower cultch volumes, the underlying biomass, size-frequency distribution, and structural stability of the reef remain highly sensitive to episodic disturbance events."








```

``` {r NumLive Models and Dataframes}
###############
### Create model
###############

### NFWF-2024 ALL Model ###
NumLive_NFWF_2024 <- glmmTMB(NumLive ~ factor(CultchDensity),
                          dispformula = ~ factor(CultchDensity), # Solves the Levene test variance shift
                          family = nbinom2,
                          data = QuadStats)
# Check goodness of fit & summary
simulateResiduals(NumLive_NFWF_2024, n = 1000, plot = T)
summary(NumLive_NFWF_2024)


###############
### Create dataframes to store values for plots and tables 
###############

# Generate Modeled Means, CI, and SE
# emmeans needed to extract values of Random effects
NumLiveStats_Subtidal_modeled <- emmeans(NumLive_NFWF_2024, ~ CultchDensity, type = "response") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename(NumLiveMean_modeled = response,
         NumLiveLower_modeled = asymp.LCL,
         NumLiveUpper_modeled = asymp.UCL) %>%
  mutate(NumLiveMeanDensity_modeled = round((NumLiveMean_modeled * 4), 1),
         NumLiveLowerDensity_modeled = round((NumLiveLower_modeled * 4), 1),
         NumLiveUpperDensity_modeled = round((NumLiveUpper_modeled * 4), 1)) %>%
  select(-df) %>%
  mutate(NumLiveUpperDensity_modeled = case_when(
    NumLiveMean_modeled <= 0 ~ 0,
    TRUE ~ NumLiveUpperDensity_modeled))

# Generate raw mean and SD
NumLiveStats_Subtidal_RAW <- QuadStats %>%
  group_by(CultchDensity) %>%
  summarise_ALL() %>%
  arrange(CultchDensity) %>%
  select(-matches("NumDrill"),
         -matches("Total"),
         -matches("Legal"))

# Combine into single table and remove intermediate dataframes
NumLiveStats_Subtidal_ALL <- left_join(NumLiveStats_Subtidal_modeled, 
                              NumLiveStats_Subtidal_RAW, 
                              by = c("CultchDensity")) 



```
